title: operator-key-custody-and-residency-assertion-middleware
author: Connor Li
release_notes: Adds operator key custody attestation middleware; exposes a feature flag for rolling rollout; documents residency proof flow and audit headers.
description: Motivation: some tenants require cryptographic proof that operator-held keys used for KMS wrapping are pinned to a jurisdiction and that operator key custody adheres to policy; this PR adds an RBACv2-aware middleware that validates operator key custody assertions against KMS attestors and enriches audit logs with residency proof metadata. Changes: 1) new middleware pkg/security/key_custody/attestor.go that validates a signed custody receipt produced by the KMS attestor service and rejects requests when custody proof does not match the tenant residency policy; 2) RBAC v2 policy extension to allow per-operator custody exemptions and timebound delegation profiles (src/rbac/v2/policy_types.go, src/rbac/v2/engine.go); 3) audit enrichment: add audit header x-residency-proof and audit fields for custody_proof_id and kms_provider in audit-writer (internal/audit/writer.go); 4) KMS integration shim that supports verifying attestation tokens from AWS KMS and a reference HSM attestor (pkg/kms/attestor_aws.go, pkg/kms/attestor_hsm.go); 5) helm chart toggle and feature flag (deploy/helm/values.yaml and charts/feature-gates.yaml) for controlled rollout; 6) e2e tests and unit tests (tests/e2e/kms_custody_test.go, tests/unit/key_custody_test.go); 7) docs and compliance playbook updates (docs/compliance/operator-key-custody.md). The description below details reviewer feedback, test matrix and rollout plan. Testing: unit tests cover 92% of attestor logic; e2e covers AWS KMS flows in staging with a mock HSM; CI includes new contract-test against the attestor API. Backwards compatibility: when the feature flag is off, behavior is unchanged and custody headers are ignored. Rollout strategy: feature-flagged canary 5% global -> 25% -> 100% with telemetry gating. Related: ENG-1983 tracks the policy schema change and SEC-44 is the compliance request from a customer. NOTE: the description is a single continuous string to satisfy PR export format.

review_comments: Aisha Khan: Can the attestor verifier accept both compact JWS and detached signatures? If not, add a compatibility shim for legacy KMS token shapes.
Connor Li: Right now the verifier accepts compact JWS and base64detached signatures; added a small compatibility layer to attestor_aws.go with a toggle guarded by the feature flag.
Miles Ortega: Audit retention teams need an immutable custody_proof_id persisted; don't rely on request headers alone. Persist to audit index and include a replay detection TTL.
Connor Li: Persisting custody_proof_id to the audit index is implemented; added replay-detection via a short-lived cache and outlined the TTL in docs (default 48h).
Priya Raman: RBAC change looks fine, but we should ensure the policy linter flags when timebound delegations are missing expiry. Add a linter rule.
Connor Li: Added linter rule src/rbac/v2/linter/timebound_checks.go and tests to ensure delegation entries include expiry. CI updated accordingly.
Security Bot (automated): gosec flagged potential weak crypto usage in attestor_hsm.go line 72; please explain reasoning or remediate.

Connor Li: The flagged code uses SHA256 over the attestation envelope per upstream HSM spec; added explicit comments and a test vector validating the envelope shape; also replaced deprecated helper in favor of crypto/hmac with constant time compare.
QA: e2e failures observed intermittently in CI on mock HSM cert rotation; added exponential backoff and retries for cert discovery in tests.
Connor Li: Increased stability of e2e tests and added retry with backoff; re-ran CI and green.
